title: Tigre Canjeero and Suqaar
community: Tigre-speaking communities of the lowland northwest
author: Chef Haile
desc: Tigre Canjeero with Suqaar — the Tigre-speaking community's fermented sorghum pancake served with a quick-cooked meat and onion scramble. Canjeero is the gateway dish between Ethiopian injera and Somali/Afar traditions — thinner than injera, cooked on both sides.
longDesc: The Tigre language (distinct from Tigrinya) is spoken by the semi-nomadic communities of northwestern Ethiopia. Their canjeero is a thin, slightly sour sorghum pancake — a bridge between injera and the canjeero of Somalia.
ingredients: // Suqaar filling: 300g minced meat, 1 onion, 1 tsp cumin, salt
steps: Mix flours, yeast, water, and salt. Ferment 8—12 hours.
Make suqaar: brown mince with onion and cumin.
Cook thin canjeero pancakes on non-stick pan — both sides.
Serve canjeero with suqaar on top.
chefTips: Canjeero is cooked on both sides — unlike injera.
commonMistakes: Too thick — canjeero should be very thin.
cookingScience: See ETH001 for sour flatbread science.
culturalNote: Tigre canjeero is the culinary bridge of northwestern Ethiopia — the place where injera culture meets the flatbread traditions of the lowland Saharan fringe.
